simple.meaning: בָּעוּ (bâʻûw) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a request.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 6:8. The surrounding contexts include Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּעוּ (H1159) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בָּעוּ (bâʻûw) / H1159 is traced through Daniel 6:8, Daniel 6:14 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it not be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn’t alter.”

timeline.evidenceText: Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it not be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn’t alter.”
Then the king, when he heard these words, was very displeased, and set his heart on Daniel to deliver him; and he labored until the going down of the sun to rescue him.
